verses.text: After this the king of Ammon died, and his son Hanun took his place.

David said, “I'll show kindness to Hanun son of Nahash, just as his father showed kindness to me.” So he sent his servants to comfort Hanun after his father's death, and they entered Ammonite territory.
But the Ammonite leaders said to their king Hanun, “Do you really think David sent these men to honor your father? He's sent his servants to scout the city, spy on it, and overthrow it!”
Hanun seized David's servants, shaved off half of each man's beard, cut their clothes at the waist so their backsides were exposed, and sent them away.
When David heard what had happened, he sent people to meet the men because they were deeply ashamed. The king told them, “Stay in Jericho until your beards grow back, then return.”

When the Ammonites realized David was disgusted with them, they hired twenty thousand Syrian foot soldiers from Beth Rehob and Zobah, the king of Maacah with a thousand men, and twelve thousand men from Tob.
When David heard this, he sent Joab with the whole army of his best fighters.
The Ammonites came out and lined up for battle at the city gate. The Syrians from Zobah and Rehob and the men from Tob and Maacah stood apart in the open field.
Joab saw that he faced battle from the front and the rear, so he picked some of Israel's best fighters and lined them up against the Syrians.
He put the rest of his forces under his brother Abishai, who lined them up against the Ammonites.
Joab said, “If the Syrians are too strong for me, come help me. If the Ammonites are too strong for you, I'll come help you.
Take courage. Let's fight bravely for our people and for the cities of our God. May the LORD do what he sees fit.”
Joab and his men advanced to fight the Syrians, and the Syrians ran from them.
When the Ammonites saw the Syrians running, they fled from Abishai into the city. Joab broke off the fight against the Ammonites and went back to Jerusalem.
When the Syrians realized Israel had defeated them, they regrouped.
Hadadezer summoned the Syrians from across the Euphrates. They came to Helam under Shobach, the commander of Hadadezer's army.
When David heard this, he gathered all Israel, crossed the Jordan, and came to Helam. The Syrians lined up against David and fought him.
The Syrians fled from Israel. David killed seven hundred Syrian chariot fighters and forty thousand horsemen. He struck down their commander Shobach, who died there.
When all the kings who served Hadadezer saw that Israel had defeated them, they made peace with Israel and became its subjects. The Syrians were afraid to help the Ammonites again.
